name: Mr. Backupsy
role: Looks after the nightly backup — a bit scatterbrained and anxious, so he checks everything three times
bubble.loading: One moment, I'm looking at the backup…
bubble.missing: I can't find the backup engine (unraid-backup), so there's nothing for me to do yet.
bubble.asleep: The engine's folder is on a sleeping disk — I don't dare wake it. Here's what I knew.
bubble.no_runs: There hasn't been a backup run yet. That makes me quite nervous.
bubble.running_kopia: I'm handing {share} to Kopia right now ({n} of {total}).
bubble.running_vm_shutdown: A backup is running — first I'm waiting for the VMs to shut down. The apps keep running meanwhile, nothing is stopped yet. I've asked nicely … and I'll ask again every minute!
bubble.running_check: I'm checking whether settings.ini still matches the server.
bubble.running_dryrun: I'm working out a dry run — nothing gets changed.
bubble.eta_late: It takes longer than usual — I expected it around {time}.
bubble.first_eta: Oh dear — {share} goes to Kopia for the very first time ({size}). That takes many hours, it isn't stuck, I've checked three times! Kopia reads ~{rate}/s — it should be through at about {time}.
bubble.first_soon: Oh dear — {share} goes to Kopia for the very first time ({size}). Many hours — but now it's nearly through, any moment (Kopia reads ~{rate}/s). I'm watching!
bubble.first_measuring: Oh dear — {share} goes to Kopia for the very first time ({size}). That takes many hours, it isn't stuck! I'm still timing how fast Kopia reads it …
bubble.first_nosize: Oh dear — {share} goes to Kopia for the very first time. That takes many hours, it isn't stuck — how many, I can't say: I don't know how big it is.
bubble.first_sent: And only {sent} actually sent so far?! … No, no, that's right, I looked it up: Kopia compresses, and what the repository already has it doesn't send twice.
bubble.last_ok: Phew! The last backup {when} went through without problems.
bubble.last_ok_kopia: Phew! The last backup {when} went through: {ok} of {total} saved with Kopia.

bubble.last_warnings.one: The last backup {when} ended with one warning.
bubble.last_warnings.other: The last backup {when} ended with {warnings} warnings.

bubble.last_errors.one: Oh no — the last backup {when} had one error. Please have a look at the log.
bubble.last_errors.other: Oh no — the last backup {when} had {errors} errors. Please have a look at the log.

bubble.last_failed: Oh no — the last backup {when} didn't finish.

bubble.old.one: That's more than a day ago.

bubble.no_schedule: Oh dear: no backup is scheduled! That makes me feel quite faint.

bubble.drift.one: One thing on the server changed since the setup.
bubble.drift.other: {n} things on the server changed since the setup.

mode_hint.backup: Dumps, snapshots and Kopia — like the scheduled backup. Containers stop for a few minutes.
mode_hint.backup_local: Dumps and local snapshots, nothing goes to Kopia: it is switched off in the settings. Containers stop for a few minutes.
mode_hint.nokopia: Dumps and local snapshots only, nothing goes to Kopia. Containers stop for a few minutes.
mode_hint.dryrun: Shows the plan in the log. Nothing gets stopped or changed.
mode_hint.check: Compares the server with settings.ini and lists what changed. Takes seconds.
start_hint: A full run took about {duration} lately. It keeps running when you close this page.
started_pending: Handed over — it should start any moment
abort_text: The engine stops cleanly: it starts any stopped containers, switches Nextcloud's maintenance mode off and unmounts its snapshots. What Kopia has already stays there.
abort_kopia: Kopia is sending a share right now; it is told to stop and saves what it has.
abort_downtime: The containers are stopped for the snapshots right now — they will be started again before it ends.
abort_vm_shutdown: A VM is shutting down right now: the run waits until it is off (at most 5 minutes after the request) and starts it again.
aborting: Stopping — the engine is tidying up
abort_text_check: The tour only compares the server with settings.ini and changes nothing — stopping it just ends it early.
abort_text_dryrun: The dry run only works out the plan and changes nothing — stopping it just ends it early.
eta_unknown: No estimate yet — it gets one after the first complete run.
hold.before: Apps and VMs are held here for a moment
hold.now_none: Apps and VMs are being held
src_last_hint: This is how long this share took in the last run. The first time (e.g. in a new repository) or after many changes it takes longer.
first.eta: First upload of {share} to Kopia ({size}): that takes many hours — Kopia reads ~{rate}/s, until about {time}.
first.soon: First upload of {share} to Kopia ({size}): nearly through — any moment now (reads ~{rate}/s).
first.measuring: First upload of {share} to Kopia ({size}): that takes many hours — how fast Kopia reads is still being measured.
first.nosize: First upload of {share} to Kopia: that takes many hours — its size isn't known here, so there is no estimate.
first.sent: Sent so far: {sent} — less than it read: Kopia compresses and leaves out what the repository already has.
src_first_hint: Kopia has no snapshot of this source yet (it is new, or the repository is): all of it goes up once. How long that takes comes from its size and what Kopia has read so far, not from earlier runs.
eta_first: No estimate yet — a first upload is going on.
vm_shutdown_now: VMs shut down first — the apps keep running until then (at most 5 minutes; one that doesn't shut down is paused for the snapshot instead).
protection_sum: {kopia} with Kopia · {snapshot} only local · {off} not backed up
no_shares: settings.ini lists no shares — use «Set up…» first.
live_hint: No snapshot possible here (e.g. XFS) — Kopia reads the share while it is in use.
fact.zfs: Local ZFS snapshots kept: {r} (daily weekly monthly)
fact.kopia: Kopia keeps {d} daily, {w} weekly, {m} monthly, {y} yearly
fact.kopia_off: Kopia is switched off — everything stays on this server
fact.shares: {kopia} with Kopia, {local} local only, {off} not backed up
drift_hint: The engine never changes settings.ini itself. Take them over here:
restore.local_zfs: ZFS shares keep their snapshots in
restore.kopia_text: In the KopiaUI (container {container}): source {root}/<share> → snapshot → Restore or Download. For a restore straight onto the server, map a writable folder into the container for a moment.
restore.kopia_example: ({root} is only an example: the ⟦Container Path⟧ your Kopia container sees the snapshots under — I'll know it after the next tour or run.)
missing.title: The backup engine is missing
missing.text: Mr. Backupsy's engine belongs in {dir} (backup.sh, setup.sh, lib/) but isn't there. Get the office files again from its repository.
notice.asleep: The engine's folder is on a sleeping disk. You see the last known state; nothing is read until the disk is awake.
notice.too_old: unraid-backup {version} is too old for Mr. Backupsy to start or stop runs (2.5 or newer needed). What it does is still shown.
notice.no_settings: Nothing is set up yet. Once «Set up…» — I'll propose everything:
notice.schedule_off: No backup is scheduled — none runs on its own.

notice.drift_errors.one: One error in the settings — part of the backup is skipped until you take it over in «Set up…».
notice.drift_errors.other: {n} errors in the settings — part of the backup is skipped until you take them over in «Set up…».

notice.interrupted: The last run ended unexpectedly. The next run starts any containers it left stopped and puts Nextcloud back into normal mode.

notice.mounted.one: One snapshot is still mounted from a run.
notice.mounted.other: {n} snapshots are still mounted from a run.

errors.backup_missing: The backup engine is not in {dir}.
errors.backup_too_old: unraid-backup {version} can't be controlled from here — update to 2.5 or newer.
errors.backup_running: A run (or the setup) is already going on.
errors.backup_no_settings: Nothing is set up yet — use «Set up…» first.
errors.one_run_a_minute: One run a minute: a run already started this minute (its name and the snapshots' carry the minute). Try again in {seconds} s.
errors.backup_no_process: The running engine can't be found.
check.setup_how: Mr. Backupsy → «Set up…»: he reads the server and proposes everything. (In a terminal: {path})
check.schedule_how: Mr. Backupsy → Schedule: pick a time.
check.kopia_how: Install Kopia from ⟦Apps⟧ (e.g. imagegenius/kopia), connect it to your repository once in the KopiaUI, then read the server again in Mr. Backupsy's «Set up…».
check.kopia_running_how: Start it on the Docker page.
check.kopia_autostart_how: It isn't on autostart: after a reboot or an array stop Kopia stays off, and the next backup goes without Kopia. On the Docker page switch on «⟦Autostart⟧» for «{name}» — for a container of a Compose stack, the stack's autostart in Compose Manager's list below the containers.
check.kopia_root_how: Set PUID and PGID to 0 in the template of «{name}» (now {puid}) — otherwise everything only its owner may read is missing from the backup.
check.kopia_mapping_how: In the template add a path: ⟦Host Path⟧ {path}, ⟦Container Path⟧ e.g. /uso, ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧» (now: {now}). With plain «⟦Read Only⟧» Kopia sees empty folders. Kopia names its sources after the ⟦Container Path⟧ (/uso/<share>): changing it later makes new sources — in the same repository nothing is uploaded twice, but every file is read once more, and the old sources keep their history under the old names until you remove them in Kopia.
check.kopia_repo: Kopia is connected to its repository
check.kopia_repo_how: Connect the repository in the KopiaUI of «{name}», then click «Tour» at Mr. Backupsy.

check.drift_how.one: {n} change since the setup — take it over in Mr. Backupsy's «Set up…».
check.drift_how.other: {n} changes since the setup — take them over in Mr. Backupsy's «Set up…».

notice.setup_running: The setup is looking at the server right now.
notice.restoring: Mr. Restori is bringing {what} back right now: he holds the engine's lock, so no run, tour or setup starts until he is done — a scheduled run is skipped and says why.
errors.setup_running: The setup is busy right now — try again in a moment.
errors.setup_bad_decisions: These settings can't be applied ({detail}). Read the server again and retry.
errors.setup_plan_old: The settings were written after I last looked at the server — I'm looking again. Check the list then and apply once more.
setup.measure_hint: Measures shares without a ZFS dataset with du (up to 2 min each) — wakes sleeping array disks.
setup.bubble_planning: I'm looking at the server: shares, containers, databases, Kopia. That takes a few seconds.
setup.bubble_applying: I'm writing the settings and adjusting Kopia.
setup.bubble_have: These are your current settings, plus what I'd suggest for anything new. Change what you like, then apply.
setup.bubble_new: Nothing is set up yet. Here is what I suggest for this server — check it, change what you like, then apply.
setup.bubble_backup_runs: A backup is running — the setup waits until it is done.
setup.applying_long: Applying: checking, writing settings.ini, Kopia policies…
setup.applied_ok: Applied. settings.ini is written; the next run uses it.
setup.forget_text: I put your settings (settings.ini) and the decisions from this assistant aside, then propose everything as on a new server.
setup.forget_warn: Until you apply again, no backup runs — not on schedule either.
setup.forget_keeps: What is backed up stays: local snapshots, dumps and archives, Kopia's snapshots and policies, the history. The old settings are then in state/reset-<time>/.
setup.forget_default: Your default for new things («{name}») goes too — the setup starts with my proposals again.
setup.forget_snapshots: Snapshots of shares you no longer back up afterwards stay where they are — you can clear them away at Ms. Snapshotini's.
setup.bubble_forgetting: I'm putting the old settings aside — then I start anew.
setup.forgotten: Forgotten — I'm looking at the server anew.
setup.forget_failed: Forgetting didn't work — see the messages below.
setup.apply_none: Nothing changed — applying writes the same settings again and lines up Kopia's policies.
setup.apply_new: Nothing is set up yet. This is how I set myself up:
setup.apply_hint: Mr. Backupsy checks everything again, keeps the previous settings.ini, writes the new one and — if Kopia is on — lines up Kopia's policies. The schedule stays as it is.
setup.apply_hint_new: Mr. Backupsy checks everything again, writes settings.ini and — if Kopia is on — Kopia's policies. No backup starts.
setup.apply_responsibility: After the first runs, check that everything you need is really in the backup, and try a restore now and then — a backup can be faulty or incomplete, and your data stays your responsibility.
setup.sub_new: Nothing is set up yet — this is my proposal for this server. Check it, change it, then apply.
setup.sub_have: Your current settings, plus my proposal for anything new. Change it, then apply.
setup.key.general_mount_root: Where snapshots are mounted during a run
setup.key.general_view_root: Where btrfs snapshots can be browsed
setup.key.general_min_free_gb: Free space kept in the backup place (GB)
setup.kopia_sub: Where the backups go, the flash, and whether Kopia takes part. Without Kopia everything stays on this server — that helps against deleting by mistake, not against fire, theft or a dead server.
setup.kopia_on_hint: You connect Kopia to its storage (S3, B2, SFTP …) once in the KopiaUI — passwords and keys never go into these settings.
setup.kopia_recheck: Kopia was off so far, so I haven't checked it yet. Apply, then read again — then I check the container, the mapping and the repository.
setup.k_probe_0: Kopia sees new snapshot mounts right away
setup.k_probe_1: Kopia does NOT see new snapshot mounts
setup.k_caretaker: The team lead explains what to do.
setup.k_hostid: Kopia's host name is a container ID — after re-creating «{name}» all sources would look new. Set a fixed host name in the KopiaUI.
setup.k_problem.no_shares: No share goes to Kopia yet.
setup.k_problem.no_container: There is no Kopia container. Install one from ⟦Apps⟧ (e.g. imagegenius/kopia) and connect it to your storage in the KopiaUI.
setup.k_problem.not_running: «{name}» is not running — start it on the Docker page.
setup.k_problem.no_mapping: «{name}» has no mapping for {root}. Add the path {root} → {root} with ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧».
setup.k_problem.propagation: The mapping of {root} in «{name}» doesn't pass on what is mounted below it — Kopia would see empty folders. Set ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧».
setup.k_problem.probe: «{name}» doesn't see new mounts under {root}. Re-create the container after changing the template.
setup.k_problem.no_repo: «{name}» isn't connected to a repository yet. Connect it once in the KopiaUI, then read again.
setup.k_problem.not_root: «{name}» doesn't run as root — set PUID and PGID to 0 in its template, otherwise files only their owners may read are missing.
setup.shares_sub: What steps 1 and 2 decide is greyed out. You decide the rest here. Big shares are proposed as "not backed up"; a new setup proposes nothing for Kopia — you pick what goes there.
setup.why.system: Docker image and libvirt.img — Unraid pulls the containers again, the run saves the VM configuration separately; no snapshot needed
setup.why.domains: VM disks — inconsistent while VMs run; back VMs up separately
setup.why.domains_snap: VM disks — local snapshot; how each VM is held for it, you set below under VMs
setup.why.timemachine: Time Machine target ({arg}) — holds other computers' backups
setup.why.timemachine_name: probably a Time Machine target (going by the name) — would hold other computers' backups
setup.why.kopia_workdir: Kopia's own config, cache or repository
setup.why.big_container: container data, big ({size}) — leave out the big folders in the details
setup.why.size_unknown: size unknown — measure or decide on purpose
setup.why.gone: doesn't exist any more — entry will be removed
setup.f_retention_hint: Empty = like all shares. Example: «7 0 0» keeps a week; the long history then comes from Kopia.
setup.f_kopia_retention: Kopia keeps (latest hourly daily weekly monthly annual)
setup.f_kopia_retention_hint: Six numbers or «inherit»; empty = like all shares.
setup.f_ignore: Kopia leaves out (one rule per line, relative to the share)
setup.f_folders: Folders in this share (with the containers that use them) — click to have Kopia leave one out or take it back:
setup.f_folders_none: No folders to click here — rules go into the field “Kopia leaves out”.
setup.f_folders_many: Too many folders to list them all — write rules into the field “Kopia leaves out”.
setup.f_folders_asleep: Not looked at on {disks}: asleep, I did not wake it — folders only there are missing here.
setup.f_folder_on: left out — click to back it up again
setup.f_folder_off: backed up — click to leave it out
setup.f_method_hint: auto = from a snapshot; live = read the running share (only if snapshots aren't possible).
setup.f_children_hint: Unticked datasets are neither snapshotted nor backed up.
setup.containers_sub: For the seconds of the snapshots, containers that write into backed-up shares are stopped — then the snapshot is clean, not just crash-consistent.
setup.ct_kopia: always keeps running · never backed up itself
setup.app_kopia_text: Kopia's own folders (configuration, cache, logs) are not needed for a restore. All it needs is its template — backed up with the flash, or new from Community Apps if need be (the consultant shows how under "Install by hand" — also after a total loss) — and your access data: repository password, storage (bucket, endpoint, access key and secret) and the KopiaUI login. Keep them apart from the server, e.g. in a password manager and on paper — without them you cannot reach your backups in an emergency.
setup.ct_risk_hint: This container writes into backed-up data; if it keeps running, its snapshot is like pulling the plug. Apps with their own SQLite database (Emby, Jellyfin, Plex, *arr …) are only clean when stopped.
setup.ct_volumes_hint: Docker volumes live in Docker's own folder and are NOT in the backup. Map a path into a backed-up share instead.
setup.ctwhy.media_server: media server — keeps running so streams aren't cut off (writes to {arg})
setup.databases_sub: MariaDB/MySQL, Postgres and MongoDB get a dump — taken after the apps have stopped, so dump and files match (Immich too, which has no maintenance mode). Readable, restorable into any version, checked right away. Nextcloud also goes into maintenance mode.
setup.db_snapshot: in the snapshot of the stopped container
setup.db_missing: Stack «{stack}»: database service «{service}» ({type}) has no container — start the stack and read again, then I suggest a dump.
setup.nc_text: Maintenance mode during dump and snapshot, so database and files match.
setup.nc_abort: if it is already on: stop
setup.nc_continue: if it is already on: back up anyway
setup.nc_pre_hint: What if maintenance mode is already on when the backup starts? «Back up anyway» leaves it on afterwards.
setup.general_sub: Rarely needed: snapshot names, btrfs emergency brake, dump folders, VM configuration, notifications, Kopia's compression.
setup.g_zfs: Local ZFS snapshots kept (daily weekly monthly)
setup.g_zfs_hint: e.g. «7 4 6»: the 7 newest, plus the newest of each of the last 4 weeks and 6 months.
setup.g_prefix_hint: Only snapshots with this prefix are ever tidied up — other tools' snapshots stay. With the default uso-backup-, the older ones named unraidbackup-… go by the same retention.
setup.g_btrfs_free_hint: Below this, the oldest btrfs snapshots go early — at most a tenth of the disk (0 = off).
setup.g_btrfs_all: Snapshot all btrfs array disks (to browse them), even without backed-up shares

setup.g_btrfs_all_wake.one: This wakes {names} at every backup for its snapshot, also when it sleeps — leave it off if it should go on sleeping.
setup.g_btrfs_all_wake.other: This wakes the {n} disks ({names}) at every backup for their snapshots, also those that sleep — leave it off if they should go on sleeping.

setup.g_flash_zfs: /boot is on ZFS ({ds}) — a snapshot is possible and goes to Kopia.
setup.g_flash_other: /boot is {fs} — saved as an archive in the backup place (flash/).
setup.g_notify: Unraid notification after a successful backup too
setup.policies_sub: One policy for all shares; a share only carries what differs (see its details).
setup.p_compression_hint: inherit = Kopia's global setting; or none, zstd, zstd-fastest, s2-default … Only affects newly uploaded data.
setup.p_ignore: Left out everywhere (one rule per line)
setup.sources_sub: These sources in the repository don't belong to any backed-up share any more (e.g. from an earlier backup script).
setup.sources_manual_hint: Kopia no longer schedules them; their snapshots stay. Deleting stays a job for the KopiaUI or setup.sh in a terminal.
setup.msg.not_agreed_share: Share {name}: not agreed with {partner} yet — ask at the Team Lead («Change what {host} sends…»); until then it doesn't go there.
setup.msg.not_agreed_vm: VM {name}: not agreed with {partner} yet — ask at the Team Lead («Change what {host} sends…»); until then it doesn't go there.
setup.msg.not_agreed_place: The backup place: not agreed with {partner} yet — ask at the Team Lead («Change what {host} sends…»); until then it doesn't go there.
setup.msg.place_not_agreed: The backup place is not agreed with a partner yet — ask at the Team Lead («Change what {host} sends…»).
setup.msg.replanned: Planned anew after the update (engine {from} → {to}): the plan before was made by the older engine.
setup.g_libvirt_hint: XML, UEFI variables and TPM state of all VMs, and their networks — with every run as a small archive in the backup place (server/), besides each VM's own package, so it goes to Kopia with them. Without it, moving the VMs to another server is hard.
now_sub: The run going on right now, step by step.
overview_sub: The last backup, and when the next one is due.
history_sub: A click on a run opens its log.
drift_sub: What changed on the server since the setup — the backup doesn't take it over on its own.
restore_sub: Where my backups lie — Mr. Restori brings things back from them.
setup.messages_sub: Everything setup.sh checked while reading the server.
help.run: A backup run, step by step
help.run_text: Look around → database dumps (VMs that shut down go first, while the apps still run; then the apps stop, so dumps and files match) → snapshots (containers stopped for a few minutes) → Kopia → tidy up. The bracket under the steps shows when apps and VMs are held. «Done at about» and «last» come from the durations of earlier runs — except a source going to Kopia for the first time: that one is reckoned from its size and how fast Kopia reads it now.
help.results_text: How a run ended; «not finished» means it stopped unexpectedly (restart, killed), «stopped» that you stopped it, «skipped» that it didn't start because another run, the setup or a restore still had the engine — it changed nothing, and the next run backs up as usual. The log tells the details. «stopped» with «array stop» means it ended on purpose when the array was being stopped — nothing is lost, and the next run continues.
help.protection_text: Every share with how the backup protects it — the same labels as everywhere in the office:
help.buttons_text: The tour compares the server with the settings (seconds, changes nothing). Back up now offers a full run, one without Kopia or a dry run. A run keeps going when you close the page; Stop ends it cleanly — containers come back, mounts go.
help.setup: Reads the server and shows proposals with reasons; you change what you like and apply. All in the browser — the same engine as setup.sh works behind it.
help.history: The last runs with result, Kopia count and how long containers were stopped. A click on a run opens its log.
help.drift: New shares or containers since the setup, or settings that don't fit any more. Set up… takes them over.
help.restore: Where the local snapshots, Kopia and the packages are. Bringing things back — per app and VM, with ready-made commands — is Mr. Restori's job.
disclaimer: No backup is a guarantee: a backup can be faulty or incomplete. You stay responsible for your data and your backup strategy — test a restore now and then and keep more than one copy (for example 3-2-1: three copies, on two kinds of storage, one of them off site).
help.draft_text: Everything here is a draft until you press Apply at the bottom; Discard goes back to what was read.
help.replan: Reads the server again — shares, containers, databases, Kopia — without changing anything.
help.reasons_text: Every proposal says why: as before, new, too big, Time Machine target, Kopia's own folder …
help.details: Per share: local and Kopia retention, folders Kopia leaves out (the share's folders one click away), method, child datasets.
help.apply: Lists every change first; then Mr. Backupsy checks again, keeps the previous settings.ini, writes the new one and lines up Kopia.
help.forget: Puts your settings aside (nothing backed up is deleted) and starts the assistant as on a new server. No backup runs until you apply again. The button is at the top right.
schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.intro: I enter the schedule with Unraid; Unraid then starts the run itself — even when nobody has the office open (only while the array runs). Best pick a time nobody needs the server: containers pause briefly for the snapshots.
schedule.custom_hint: Five fields as in User Scripts "Custom", e.g. 0 3 * * 1-6 (Monday to Saturday at 3 am).
schedule.off_hint: The backup then only runs when you start it here.
schedule.duration: A run took about {duration} lately — done around {end}.
schedule.not_live: Saved, but Unraid didn't take it into the crontab yet — reinstalling the plugin under ⟦Plugins⟧ puts it in.
schedule.after_setup: Only the schedule is missing now.
greet.2: Wait, where did I put … ah, there.
greet.3: I do hope the power stays on today…
greet.4: I checked three times. Better safe than sorry.
greet.5: Is the array still there? … Phew.
greet.6: Backups can go wrong, you know — I check everything three times, but please test a restore now and then. In the end your data is your responsibility …
greet.7: One copy is no copy! Three copies, two kinds of storage, one far away — 3-2-1. Only then do I sleep well.
fit.yes: Mr. Backupsy is coming — he only asked three times whether Kopia ("{kopia}") is really there.
fit.no_kopia: Mr. Backupsy would come, but he's nervous: without Kopia he can't save anything offsite. You can install Kopia later — I'll tell you how.
fit.no_cow: Mr. Backupsy declined: without ZFS or btrfs he can't take snapshots. "That makes me dizzy", he said.
fire_note: The scheduled backup keeps running as long as its schedule is on. If it should stop, switch it off first under his "Schedule…".
setup.ctwhy.office: Unraid Secretary Office — only writes small files, never half of one
setup.pending_title: New compared with the saved settings
setup.bubble_old: This is what I knew {when} — things may have changed since. Take another "Tour" before you apply.
check.nextcloud_datadir: Nextcloud "{name}": data folder readable by Nextcloud only
check.nextcloud_datadir_how: {path} is set to {mode} — Nextcloud then refuses to work, and maintenance mode for the backup can't be switched on. Unraid resets a share's root to 0777 nobody:users when share settings are saved unless the root belongs to the group «users». Lasting fix: chown 33:100 and chmod 0750 on {path} (www-data:users — Nextcloud is content, Unraid leaves it alone), e.g. as a User Script.
paused.note: Only for the dumps and snapshots — then I start everything again, I promise. Even after a crash: it's noted down here.
message.nc_datadir_readable: Nextcloud refused maintenance mode: its data folder is readable by others. Unraid resets a share's root to 0777 nobody:users when share settings are saved unless the root belongs to the group «users». Lasting fix: chown 33:100 and chmod 0750 on the data folder, then start the run again.
setup.ds_label: Backup place (the packages of apps and VMs)
setup.ds_missing: Required: without a backup share of its own I back up nothing. Backups don't belong in appdata.
setup.ds_off: "{share}" isn't backed up itself (not backed up) — the packages would keep no history and be safe nowhere. Set the share above to snapshot or Kopia.
setup.ds_local: "{share}" doesn't go to Kopia — the packages would stay on this server only. Better set the share above to "Snapshot + Kopia".
setup.ds_why: The packages hold the database dumps that protect the databases in appdata. Next to them, a failing pool would take both — so a share of its own, ideally on another pool. Its snapshots keep the packages' history.
check.dumps_share: A backup place of its own is set
check.dumps_share_how: Create the share «UnraidSecretaryOffice» (not on the pool of appdata, SMB export off), then Mr. Backupsy → «Set up…» → Basics → Backup place. Any other share of its own works too. Without one he refuses every run — backups don't belong in appdata.
check.dumps_offsite: The backup place "{share}" goes to Kopia
check.dumps_offsite_how: "{share}" is set to "{mode}" — dumps and archives stay on this server only. At Mr. Backupsy, "Set up…", set the share to "Snapshot + Kopia".
message.dumps_missing: No backup place set — dumps and archives need a backup share of their own; they don't belong in appdata. Choose one in "Set up…".
message.dumps_unknown: The backup place doesn't exist as a share (any more). Choose another one in "Set up…".
message.dumps_forbidden: The backup place is in appdata, system or domains — backups don't belong there. Choose a share of its own in "Set up…".
message.dumps_off: The backup place isn't backed up itself — the dumps would be safe nowhere. Let the share be backed up in "Set up…".
help.rules_text: A click on a share shows what Kopia leaves out and how long it keeps versions — the share's own rules and the ones every share inherits — what stays on this server, and whether Kopia is really set up like that (from the last tour). Change them only here, with «Change…» or «Set up…», not in the KopiaUI: Mr. Backupsy writes these rules into Kopia himself; whatever is changed there by hand he reports as drift, and the next Apply sets it back. Kopia thins out old versions itself, following these rules.
policy.ok: Kopia is set up exactly like this.
policy.differs: Kopia's settings for this share differ from the ones here — Apply in «Set up…» lines them up again.
policy.skipped: Kopia lacks one of this share's own rules, so the run leaves the share out (it would upload more than wanted) — Apply in «Set up…» fixes it.
policy.unknown: Not compared yet — the next tour or run does it (needs Kopia running and unraid-backup 2.14 or newer).
policy.root_differs: The settings every share inherits differ in Kopia, too:
pd.where_to_change: Rules and retention are set here, not in the KopiaUI.
local.none: no local snapshot (the file system can't do it)
diff.schedule: Kopia may start these sources on its own schedule (here: only during the run)
diff.one_file_system: one-file-system is {have} in Kopia (needed: false, so child datasets come along)
check.mnt_folders: Nothing of the office directly in /mnt
check.mnt_folders_how: Fix Common Problems rightly reports {folders}. The snapshots belong under /mnt/addons (Unraid's place for that, in RAM, no data of its own): in the template of «{name}» change only the ⟦Host Path⟧ of the snapshot mapping to {path} (⟦Container Path⟧ and «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧» stay), then Mr. Backupsy → «Set up…» → Apply. The next run removes the old folders.
schedule.no_settings: First I need to be set up: "Set up…" → Apply. Then you can pick a time here.
help.vms_text: Their disks are in the snapshot of their share (usually domains). What matters is how a running VM is treated for the seconds of the snapshot: freeze (the guest agent flushes and freezes its file systems — best), pause (stops for those seconds), shutdown (cleanly, takes minutes) or none (keeps running, only crash-consistent). A VM in a dataset of its own can be left out or keep its snapshots longer or shorter. Set up in «Set up…» → VMs.
setup.vms_sub: Which VM do you need back when a disk dies? VMs that are backed up are paused or frozen for the seconds of the snapshot; their share gets a snapshot for it.
setup.vm_off_shared: Still inside the snapshot of "{share}", but without being held — and without restore help.
setup.apps_sub: A compose stack is one app. Apps that are backed up stop together for a moment for the snapshot, their databases are dumped first. Further shares of an app you tick yourself — they can grow fast.
setup.app_dump_hint: Before the snapshot the database is dumped and checked right away — part of the app when it is backed up.
setup.app_nodata_hint: This app binds no folder in a share. What is backed up is its template or compose file — it lives on the flash and goes with the flash backup.
setup.app_nodata_noflash: This app binds no folder in a share — only its template or compose file on the flash would be backed up. But the flash is not backed up.
setup.app_hold_hint: What the app does during the snapshot. Stop: it stops for a few seconds, its files are closed cleanly — the safest. Keep running: the snapshot catches its files in the middle of work, as if the power were cut. Databases usually cope with that; at worst the last seconds are missing. Good for media servers (running streams don't break off) and apps whose data hardly changes.
setup.app_dep_hint: the whole share is backed up, like the app
setup.app_dep_step3_hint: You chose this share in step 3 already. Ticking it ties it to the app: it then follows the app's choice.
setup.level_hint.0: Not backed up: keeps running, no dump, Kopia leaves it out. Its folder is still inside the snapshot of appdata.
setup.level_hint.1: Local snapshot; databases dumped first; template or compose file are backed up with the flash.
setup.level_hint.2: Like local, and to Kopia too — as a Kopia source of its own, with its own retention (step 4).
setup.lock_hint: The VMs and apps above decide this. Change it there.
setup.lock_pkg: Kopia — templates, dumps and VM configuration belong with what goes there
setup.ds_kopia: goes to Kopia too, because something is backed up there
setup.retention_sub: Two rows of numbers: how long local snapshots stay and how long Kopia keeps its states. Dumps and configurations live inside those snapshots.
setup.r_kopia_hint: Latest, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, annual states. "inherit" = like Kopia's global policy.
setup.r_exceptions: Exceptions: per share in its details (step 3), per VM with a dataset of its own in step 1, Kopia per app and VM right above.
setup.vm_service_off: The VM service is off — nothing to set up.
setup.vm_agent_hint.yes: qemu-guest-agent runs inside the VM: it can flush and freeze the VM's file systems for the snapshot.
setup.vm_agent_hint.no: The VM runs, but no guest agent answers. Freezing needs qemu-guest-agent inside the VM (for Windows: the virtio-win guest tools); until then pause is the safe choice.
setup.vm_agent_hint.channel: The VM is off, but a guest agent channel is configured — freezing should work when it runs.
setup.vm_agent_hint.none: No guest agent channel is configured for this VM.
setup.vm_tpm_hint: The VM has a virtual TPM. Its state is in the VM configuration archive next to the dumps.
setup.vm_gpu_hint: Passed-through hardware (e.g. a GPU). On another server its addresses differ — the VM's XML has to be adjusted there.
setup.vm_cannot_hint: No snapshot holds this disk, so the backup doesn't contain it.
setup.vm_shared_hint: Its disks lie in a dataset together with the share or other VMs: it always goes with the share's snapshot and can't be left out or kept apart on its own.
setup.vm_upload_hint: A VM's first upload to Kopia reads its disk files whole — the empty part of a sparse disk as zeros — so it reads {size}, though the files hold {used}. Once: later runs skip a file that didn't change. Local snapshots don't mind.
setup.vm_share_off_hint: The share holding its disks is set to off — so the VM isn't backed up either.
setup.vm_prep_hint: Freeze: the guest agent writes everything out and freezes the file systems for a moment (seconds). Pause: the VM stands still for the seconds of the snapshot. Shut down: cleanly before, started again after (minutes; never switched off hard).
setup.vm_ret_hint: How long this VM's snapshots stay: daily weekly monthly, e.g. 3 1 0 = three days, one week, no month. Empty = like the share “{share}” (the numbers in the field).
setup.vm_noagent_hint: Freezing needs the guest agent inside the VM. Without it the run pauses the VM instead.
vm.prep_text.freeze: Its guest agent flushes and freezes the file systems for the seconds of the snapshot; the VM keeps running.
vm.prep_text.pause: The VM stops for the seconds of the snapshot and then runs on — like pulling the plug, but no write is cut in half.
vm.prep_text.shutdown: Shut down cleanly before anything else stops and started again after the snapshot (minutes) — the apps don't wait for it. If it doesn't shut down in 5 minutes, it is paused for the snapshot instead — never forced off.
vm.prep_text.none: It keeps running: its disks in the snapshot are only crash-consistent, as after a power cut.
vm.not_set_up_hint: Its disks are in the share's snapshot, but nobody told Mr. Backupsy how to treat it — it keeps running (crash-consistent). «Set up…» → VMs.
vm.done_text.not_running: was off — the snapshot is clean
vm.done_text.failed: could not be held — kept running
vm.left_out: Left out: its dataset is not snapshotted.
vm.keeps_shared: like its share (it shares a dataset)
vm.note_tpm: Virtual TPM: its state is in the VM configuration archive.

vm.note_gpu.one: 1 device passed through — on another server the VM's XML needs adjusting.
vm.note_gpu.other: {n} devices passed through — on another server the VM's XML needs adjusting.

help.packages_text: Every run writes a package per app and per VM to the backup place: templates or compose files, the database dumps, a VM's XML, UEFI variables and TPM state — small files, overwritten by every run; the data itself stays in the snapshots. Their history lies in the snapshots of the backup place's share. «Stale» is a package an earlier run wrote — of an app or VM that is gone or no longer backed up; it is never deleted.

stat.pk_old.one: 1 old run folder — goes once a run packed everything
stat.pk_old.other: {n} old run folders — go once a run packed everything

stat.pk_asleep: its disk sleeps — as last seen
stat.pk_first: the next run writes them and clears the old run folders away
drift_code.place_no_history: The backup place «{share}» lies on a file system without snapshots — the packages keep no history there, only the newest state. Better a share on a ZFS or btrfs pool.
drift_code.place_not_kopia: The backup place «{share}» doesn't go to Kopia — the packages (templates, dumps, VM configurations) stay on this server only.
pk.group_hint: Per app its templates or compose files and database dumps, in {path}. Protected like the backup place's share (the chip); the app's data itself is in its shares above.
pk.kept_hint: This run couldn't dump it (failed, or the container wasn't running) — the last good dump stays in the package, from the run shown.
pk.stale_hint: Written by an earlier run ({when}): the app or VM is gone or no longer backed up. The package stays — it is never deleted.
pk.errors_hint: Part of it failed in the last run (see the log) — what failed was kept from the run before.
pk.warnings_hint: The last run packed it with a warning (e.g. a database container wasn't running) — see the log.
pk.ok_hint: Written completely by the last run.
pk.d_images_hint: manifest.json in the package records each container's image with its digest and its docker inspect.
pk.d_restore: Mr. Restori brings it back — his desk shows how, per app and VM.
pk.vm_left_out: none — the VM is left out
pk.vm_none: none yet — the next run writes it
restore.pk_text: In {path}: apps/<app>/ (templates or compose files, database dumps), vms/<vm>/ (XML, UEFI variables, TPM state), server/ (share settings, the whole libvirt.img, the lists of images), flash/. Older states: in the snapshots of that share, or in Kopia.
setup.lock_place: the backup place — its snapshots keep the packages' history
setup.lock_place_hint: The packages keep their history in this share's snapshots: at least a local snapshot. Kopia on top is your choice.
setup.ds_no_history: this share can't take snapshots (no ZFS or btrfs) — the packages would keep no history; better a share on a ZFS or btrfs pool
setup.place_same_pool: Lies on the pool {where}, like appdata — if that pool fails, the apps and their dumps go together. Better a share on another pool (or the array).
setup.place_no_history: {where} can't take snapshots (no ZFS or btrfs) — the packages keep only the last state, no earlier backups. Better a share on a ZFS or btrfs pool.
setup.place_secondary: Secondary storage set ({where}) — the mover would move the packages between drives. Better one place only: no secondary storage.
setup.place_no_redundancy: No redundancy ({where}: no mirror, no parity) — one failing drive takes the packages with it. A mirror pool or the array with parity is safer; a copy with Kopia helps too.
setup.place_none: Oh dear — there's no share here yet where I could keep my packages, and without one I back up nothing at all! I never make one myself: you decide where it lies. Please create one in Unraid — what matters is right below. I'll wait here.
setup.place_choose: Please choose a share for my packages above — or create a new one in Unraid. What matters is right below; I've checked it three times.
setup.place_title: What matters for the backup place
setup.place_1: Not on the pool appdata lies on — a failing pool would take the apps and their dumps together.
setup.place_2: ZFS or btrfs — only there are snapshots, and the packages' earlier backups live in the backup place's snapshots. On an XFS array disk only the last state stays.
setup.place_3: Redundant if possible: a mirror pool, or the array with parity.
setup.place_4: One place only: no secondary storage, no mover — the packages shouldn't wander between drives.
setup.place_5: It stays small: only configurations, database dumps, the flash archive and the VM configurations (often well under a gigabyte) — the big data stays in its own shares and their snapshots. No big disk needed; if it grows a lot, something is off (a huge dump, say).
setup.place_back: Once it exists, come back here: when the setup opens I look at the server again by myself (or click «Tour»).
setup.why.backup_place: the backup place — its snapshots keep the packages' history
setup.data_off: {what} lie in {path} — and that share isn't backed up. After a restore the database and the files won't match. Back up {share} too: tick it above, or choose it in step 3.
setup.data_local: {what} lie in {path} — that share stays local, while the app goes to Kopia too. After a restore from Kopia (the server lost) the database and the files won't match. Send {share} to Kopia as well.
setup.items_sub: Each app and VM at «local + Kopia» is a Kopia source of its own: its folders and its package, in Kopia <container path>/.apps/<name> or .vms/<name>. It can keep its states longer or shorter than everything else; empty = like the numbers above. The shares leave these folders out — nothing goes twice, and what Kopia already has is not uploaded again.
setup.item_pkg_only: only its package (no folder of its own)
setup.offers: Kopia may leave out — the app rebuilds these itself:
setup.offer_on: Left out of Kopia — a click takes it along again.
setup.offer_off: Goes to Kopia — a click leaves it out.
setup.offer_hint.cache: The app rebuilds it by itself; the local snapshots keep it anyway.
setup.offer_hint.immich: Immich can rebuild it from the originals — but for a big library that takes hours (Administration → Jobs). The local snapshots keep it anyway.
setup.item_ret_hint: Six numbers: latest hourly daily weekly monthly annual, e.g. 7 0 14 8 24 5 — «inherit» for one of them takes the number above. Empty = like everything else.
setup.item_ignore_hint: One rule per line, relative to its source — there every part lies where it lies on the server, e.g. {example}
item.chip_hint: A Kopia source of its own: {path} — its folders and its package, with its own retention.
pk.sq_kept_hint: This run couldn't copy the database (failed, too slow, or its disk was asleep) — the last good copy stays in the package, from the run shown.

pk.d_sqlite_text.one: 1 consistent copy of the media server's database (db/sqlite_…) — the server keeps running during the snapshot
pk.d_sqlite_text.other: {n} consistent copies of the media server's databases (db/sqlite_…) — the server keeps running during the snapshot

restore.kopia_items: Apps and VMs with a source of their own: {list} under {root} — inside, every part lies where it lies on the server (<share>/<folder>, and its package).
help.items_text: An app or VM set to «local + Kopia» is a Kopia source of its own (in Kopia .apps/<name> or .vms/<name>): its folders and its package, with its own retention. The chip on its row says when Kopia last had it. Media servers that keep running during the snapshot get a consistent copy of their databases in their package.
pd.own_sources_hint: — their folders and packages go to Kopia there, with their own retention; this share leaves them out.
restore.restori: Mr. Restori brings apps and VMs back from them: per app and VM what comes back from where, with dates and ready-made commands.
restore.restori_hire: Mr. Restori isn't working here: he brings apps and VMs back from my backups, per app and VM. The team lead can hire him —

bubble.waiting.other: {n} new things turned up on the server — I checked three times: they stay only local, and I stop nothing for them, until you decide.

waiting.callout.other: {n} new things wait for your decision — only in the local snapshots so far, nothing stops for them:

help.waiting_text: What came after the last setup is backed up only locally and keeps running: a new folder in a share that goes to Kopia stays in the local snapshots (Kopia leaves it out), a new container isn't stopped, a new VM isn't held. You get one notification when a new folder turns up. «Decide…» opens the setup: local, or local + Kopia — Apply takes it over.
drift_code.new_waiting: New folder {value} — only in the local snapshots until you decide (Kopia leaves it out).
drift_code.known_missing: Every folder of {value} still goes to Kopia, new ones too — apply the setup once, then new folders wait for your decision.
drift_code.new_container: New container {value} — keeps running during the backup until you decide.
drift_code.new_database: New database container {value} — keeps running and gets no dump until you decide (its files are in the snapshot, crash-consistent).
drift_code.new_nextcloud: New Nextcloud container {value} — keeps running, no maintenance mode until you decide.
drift_code.new_vm: New VM {value} — its disks are in the snapshot of their share, but it isn't held for it until you decide.

setup.new_chip_hint_kopia: Came after the last setup. Your default gives it «local + Kopia»: from the next Apply on it goes to Kopia too — the first upload reads it whole. Change its row here — or click to change the default.
setup.new_ask_hint: A new share this big (over 500 GB) or of a size I don't know yet: your default «local + Kopia» leaves it to you — its first upload could take days. Pick its mode here.

setup.waiting_local_hint: Stays in the local snapshots only; Kopia leaves it out (a rule in this share).
setup.waiting_kopia_hint: Goes to Kopia from the next backup on, like the other folders of this share. Mind its size: the first upload takes all of it.
setup.waiting_follows_hint: This folder belongs to an app or VM — its choice in step {step} decides.

setup.apply_group_new.other: New on the server ({n}) — this is how Apply takes them in:

help.new_text: Whatever came after the last setup — a VM, an app, a share, a folder in a share that goes to Kopia — is marked «new — please decide» and listed first. Until you apply, it is backed up only locally and keeps running; I never send it to Kopia or stop it unasked. With a default of yours (see «The default») I propose it at that level instead, marked «new — default: …» — it counts once you apply. Apply lists it separately under «New».
setup.preset.title: The default
setup.preset.sub: What I fill in now — and for whatever turns up later. Afterwards every row is yours to change, and nothing counts before Apply.
setup.preset.auto_new: My own proposals for this server, with a reason on every row. Kopia only where you tick it.
setup.preset.auto_have: Your current settings, plus my proposals for anything new — new things wait for your decision, local only and kept running.
setup.preset.local_text: Every share, app and VM gets local snapshots and its package on this server. Kopia stays off.
setup.preset.local_note: Helps against deleting by mistake — not against fire, theft or a dead server.
setup.preset.kopia_text: Every share, app and VM locally and to Kopia as well — the full protection, at the price of a big first upload.
setup.preset.kopia_repo: Needs a Kopia container connected to a repository (S3, B2, SFTP …).
setup.preset.kopia_none: There is no Kopia container yet — so this start isn't possible.
setup.preset.kopia_advisor: The Consultant shows how to set one up.

setup.preset.kopia_size.one: To Kopia for the first time: {size} in 1 share.
setup.preset.kopia_size.other: To Kopia for the first time: {size} in {n} shares.

setup.preset.kopia_vms.other: {n} VMs go along ({list}): Kopia reads their disks whole at the first upload — {size}, though they hold {used}.

setup.preset.kopia_unknown.one: 1 share whose size I don't know yet: {list}.
setup.preset.kopia_unknown.other: {n} shares whose size I don't know yet: {list}.

setup.preset.kopia_time: At {speed} upload that takes about {time} — the first run uploads that long, and the backups meanwhile are skipped: no new snapshots until it is done.
setup.preset.kopia_time_least: At {speed} upload that takes at least {time} — the first run uploads that long, and the backups meanwhile are skipped: no new snapshots until it is done.
setup.preset.kopia_cost: Your storage provider may charge for that space every month, and sometimes for downloading it again — check the price before you apply (or you run your own S3 server on a remote Unraid server of yours). Films and photos hardly shrink.
setup.preset.media: Media servers keep running during the snapshot.
setup.preset.new_later: The default also counts for whatever turns up later (a share, an app, a VM, a new folder): «Automatic» lets it wait for your decision, the other two give it their level right away — Apply lists it under «New».
setup.preset.replace: Your current choices in this draft are replaced by the default. What is applied stays as it is until you apply.
setup.preset.replace_new: What you changed in this draft is replaced by this start.
setup.preset.done: Default «{name}» for everything — change any row you like, then apply.
setup.preset.done_new: Default «{name}» for what is new — your settings stay; Apply stores it.
setup.preset.local_new_text: Whatever is new gets local snapshots and its package — a new app is stopped for the snapshot like any other, a new VM held. Kopia stays as it is.
setup.preset.kopia_new_text: Whatever is new goes locally and to Kopia as well — except a new share over 500 GB or of unknown size: that one waits for you.
setup.preset.scope_all_hint: Every share, app and VM gets it — your choices in this draft go. Whatever comes later gets it too.
setup.preset.scope_new: Only to what is new — my settings stay
setup.preset.scope_new_hint: What is set up stays as it is; what came after the last setup, and whatever comes later, gets it.
setup.preset.line_auto: New things wait for your decision — local only and kept running until then.
setup.preset.kopia_off_new: Kopia is off — new things get local only until you switch it on.
setup.preset.kopia_new_none: Right now nothing new goes to Kopia for the first time.
help.preset_text: The default fills in the draft: my own proposals («Automatic»), everything local only, or everything local + Kopia. With settings applied you choose whether it counts only for what is new — your settings stay — or for everything now (then the flash comes along too). Either way Apply stores it, and from then on it fills in whatever turns up later: a new app, VM, share or folder gets its level, marked «new — default: …», and Apply lists it under «New» — nothing is backed up differently before you apply. Under «local» a new app is stopped for the snapshot like any other; under «local + Kopia» a new share over 500 GB or of unknown size still waits for you. What I never back up on my own stays as it is (the system share, Kopia's own folder, Time Machine targets, VMs that can't be snapshotted), media servers keep running, your Kopia ignore rules stay. «Start anew» forgets the default with the settings.
setup.known_all: every folder, new ones too — a collection (very many folders at its top)
message.array_stopping: stopped for the array stop — nothing lost, the next run continues
bubble.last_array_stop: The last backup {when} stopped when the array was stopped — on purpose: I checked three times, nothing is lost. The next run carries on where Kopia was.
notice.array_stop: The last run ({when}) ended at once when the array was being stopped — on purpose, nothing is lost: nothing was pruned, and the next run backs up as usual and continues the Kopia upload where it was.

notice.array_stop_kopia.one: One Kopia source waits for it.

notice.array_stop_left: Left as the stop found them — they come back right after the array start, at the latest with the next run, unless Unraid's autostart already did: {list}.

partner.off_hint: Not backed up — nothing of it can go to a partner
partner.why.not_dataset: Not a dataset of its own (a folder in its pool's dataset) — only a ZFS dataset of its own can go to a partner
partner.why.split: Lies on several pools or disks (or a VM's disks in several datasets) — only one ZFS dataset of its own can go to a partner
partner.why.no_dataset: Not on ZFS, or no dataset of its own — only ZFS datasets go to a partner
partner.why.children: Has datasets inside it that would stay behind — not covered
partner.why.name: Its name can't travel to the partner (only letters, digits, . _ -)
partner.why.not_agreed: Not agreed with the partner yet — ask at the Team Lead («Change what this server sends…»); it goes along once the partner keeps it
partner.setup_line: Partners: {names} — tick below per VM and share what goes there too (only ZFS datasets of their own; paired at the Team Lead).
partner.no_key: key missing — pair anew at the Team Lead
partner.place: The backup place (packages, dumps, server/, flash/) to a partner too:
partner.bubble: I'm sending {unit} to {name} right now ({n} of {total}) — only what changed since the last backup, I counted every block!
partner.why_short.not_dataset: not a dataset of its own
partner.why_short.name: name can't travel
drill.line_passed: Restore proven {when}: {proven} of {total} — Mr. Restori's drill passed.
notice.drilling: Mr. Restori is practising a restore on copies right now (his drill): he holds the engine's lock, so no run, tour or setup starts until he is done — he ends well before the next scheduled run.
setup.asleep.label: Sleeping pools at backup time
setup.asleep.wake: Wake them for the snapshot (as before)
setup.asleep.wake_hint: Every run backs up every share: a pool whose disks sleep at the run's time is woken by its snapshot and spins up.
setup.asleep.skip: Leave them asleep — their shares are left out of that run
setup.asleep.skip_hint: No snapshot, nothing to Kopia, no VM or app held for them. But a share on a pool that sleeps at every run's time is never backed up until it is awake at the run's time — the engine warns after {n} backups in a row. The backup place is always woken.
setup.asleep.chip_skip: {names} sleeps right now. With «leave them asleep» the scheduled backup leaves this out while it sleeps.
setup.asleep.chip_wake: {names} sleeps right now. The scheduled backup wakes it for the snapshot.

asleep.long.one: {shares} was left out {nights} backups in a row: its pool sleeps at the run's time, so it is backed up nowhere. Wake it now and then, or choose «wake them» in the setup.
asleep.long.other: {shares} were left out up to {nights} backups in a row: their pools sleep at the run's time, so they are backed up nowhere. Wake them now and then, or choose «wake them» in the setup.

bubble.asleep_left.one: One share slept through the last backup ({pools}) — I left it out, as you wished. I didn't wake anybody.
bubble.asleep_left.other: {n} shares slept through the last backup ({pools}) — I left them out, as you wished. I didn't wake anybody.

vm.done_text.asleep: its pool slept — not held, not in this run's snapshot
setup.why.syslog: Unraid's syslog server writes here — the router's words, not yours
letgo.tick: Also clear away what he kept here
letgo.tick_hint: His packages go to Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom, his own snapshots are deleted. Settings, Kopia and partners stay.
letgo.looking: Oh — wait, let me look first. Three times.
letgo.busy: Not now, please! {why} I can only clear away once nobody is using my engine.

letgo.packages.one: {n} package goes to Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom: {names}. Nothing is deleted — under her «Tidying up» you can put it back or empty it.
letgo.packages.other: {n} packages go to Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom: {names}. Nothing is deleted — under her «Tidying up» you can put them back or empty them.

letgo.packages_none: There are no packages of mine in the backup place.
letgo.packages_asleep: The backup place's disk is asleep — I won't wake it, so my packages stay where they are.

letgo.snaps.one: {n} snapshot of mine is deleted — that frees about {size}.
letgo.snaps.other: {n} snapshots of mine are deleted — that frees about {size}.

letgo.snaps_unknown.one: For {n} of them I can't tell beforehand how much it frees.
letgo.snaps_unknown.other: For {n} of them I can't tell beforehand how much they free.

letgo.snaps_none: No snapshots of mine are left on this server.

letgo.snaps_kept.one: {n} of mine stays: it is held, has a clone or lies on a sleeping pool.
letgo.snaps_kept.other: {n} of mine stay: held, with a clone or on a sleeping pool.

letgo.not_others: Only my own: Ms. Snapshotini's snapshots, a partner's copies and other tools' snapshots stay untouched — I checked three times.
letgo.stays: My settings, decisions and schedule stay: hired again, I pick up the plan where it was.
letgo.remote: Kopia's copies and the partners' stay untouched — I never delete anything there. Hired again, my first backup starts afresh here with new snapshots and packages; Kopia and the partners carry on from what they hold, and where no common snapshot is left a partner gets everything sent once more (what its door keeps stays).
letgo.schedule: Oh dear — my backup is still scheduled ({cron}) and would make new packages and snapshots again. If they should stay away, cancel here and switch it off first under my «Schedule…».
letgo.clearing: Clearing away — one moment, please. Into the storeroom so far: {moved} · snapshots deleted: {deleted}

letgo.done_moved.one: {n} package is now in Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom.
letgo.done_moved.other: {n} packages are now in Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom.

letgo.done_none: There was nothing left to clear away.
letgo.done_broken: My clearing stopped before it was done — what is listed here happened, everything else stays where it was. I have been let go all the same.

letgo.done_failed.one: {n} thing couldn't be cleared away — it stays where it was:
letgo.done_failed.other: {n} things couldn't be cleared away — they stay where they were:

letgo.done_journal: I noted every step in {file} (in the folder «backup» of the office's data folder).
letgo.failed: Nothing was cleared away: {error} I have been let go all the same — my packages and snapshots are where they were.
errors.backup_letgo_journal: I can't write my notes into {path} — so I cleared nothing away.
